headline: Texas hemp sellers eye reset after Goodwin ousts Dan Patrick
dek: Texas's new Democratic leaders back THC access, but state rules, court cases and the federal hemp ban due 11 December mean shelves will not refill soon.
key_points: Lt. Gov. Dan Patrick, who led the push to ban hemp THC in Texas, lost on 3 November to Democrat Vikki Goodwin, who campaigned on undoing the restrictions.
Gov.-elect Gina Hinojosa has criticised the state's THC rules and promised Texans a vote on the future of THC.
State health rules in force since 31 March cap total THC at 0.3% and raised licence fees to as much as $10,000, wiping out smokable hemp in many shops.
The legislature meets on 12 January, but THCA flower also fails the federal total THC test that takes effect on 11 December.
body: Texas's hemp industry spent two years fighting Lt. Gov. Dan Patrick. On 3 November voters removed him. Democrat Vikki Goodwin, an Austin state representative, beat the incumbent by about six points, KSAT reported, after a campaign that put his push against hemp-derived THC near the centre. Democrat Gina Hinojosa won the governor's race, and Democrats also gained a majority in the Texas House, according to Marijuana Moment.

The industry is reading the result as a mandate. The people who will have to turn it into law are more cautious: the state's current hemp rules, pending court cases and a federal ban on most intoxicating hemp products all stand between the election night mood and products returning to shelves.
## How THC got on the ballot

Patrick made a ban on hemp-derived THC a top priority in 2025. The legislature passed it; Abbott vetoed it, though he signed a separate ban on THC vapes. State regulators then tightened the market anyway. Rules from the Texas Department of State Health Services, in force since 31 March, require child-resistant packaging, new labelling, testing and record-keeping, and set a minimum buying age of 21, according to The Texas Tribune.

The rules also set a 0.3% total THC limit that retailers said would eliminate smokable products such as pre-rolls and flower, which they said make up more than half of some stores' stock. Manufacturer licence fees rose from $258 to $10,000 per facility, and retail registrations from $155 to $5,000.

Every major Democratic campaign, including Goodwin's, Hinojosa's and that of US Senate winner James Talarico, made hemp an issue, according to industry advocates quoted by the Tribune. Texas Majority PAC's executive director said THC was one of several issues that moved voters, and a Rice University political scientist described it as one factor among many in an unfavourable national climate for the party in power.

Goodwin's published cannabis priorities include legalizing cannabis, hemp and THC, reversing the regulatory crackdown, and regulating with age limits, labelling and testing standards, KSAT reported. She also campaigned on using sales tax revenue from THC products to fund health coverage for low-income Texans. Hinojosa has criticised the state's regulations and promised Texans a vote on the future of THC.

Mark Bordas, executive director of the Texas Hemp Business Council, told KSAT his group had already been in contact with Goodwin's team. Asked how likely it was that the full range of hemp THC products returns, he put it at about seven in ten.
> The election changed who holds the gavel in Texas, not what is legal on Monday morning.
## Why it will not be quick

The lieutenant governor's power comes from running the state Senate, and that chamber still has Republicans who want hemp banned. Katharine Neill Harris, a drug policy fellow at Rice University's Baker Institute, told the Tribune that Goodwin will need legislative support, that Hinojosa could block new ban attempts, and that Senate Republicans may try to strip the lieutenant governor of some of the power Patrick used.

Harris also said she saw no sign that state health regulators would change their rules on their own, though litigation over the THCA rule is ongoing and the court hearing it may change composition after judicial races. Retailers expect a friendlier bench. Harris argued that legislation would be sturdier than piecemeal rules because it is less exposed to lawsuits.

Then there is Washington. Shayda Torabi, co-founder of Austin retailer RESTART CBD, warned that even if Texas lifts its smokable ban, THCA flower fails the new federal total THC test from 11 December. Smokable products would need either a federal reversal or a state-legal market built by lawmakers. Bordas told KSAT he does not expect federal or state enforcement against a Texas framework, but that is his view, not a legal position.

Some officials want to go further. San Antonio Councilman Jalen McKee-Rodriguez has asked the city to study the economic impact of legalizing cannabis, with the aim of making the case to state lawmakers, KSAT reported. Harris noted that Texas could create a full legal cannabis market, as 24 other states have, and route smokable products through it. Marijuana possession remains illegal under Texas law.

The legislature convenes on 12 January. Watch the Senate's rules vote, which will show how much power Goodwin actually holds; the first hemp or cannabis bills filed; any movement in the THCA rule litigation; and whether Congress changes the federal hemp definition before 11 December. For hemp sellers, the honest timeline is months, not weeks.
